title: A weak shock passes a cylinder of light or heavy gas
question: A planar shock at Mach 1.22 runs through air in a shock tube and meets a cylinder of another gas, held by a thin membrane, its axis across the tube. The shock refracts into the cylinder, a transmitted shock emerges behind it, and the cylinder is set in motion and deformed. Report three speeds measured along the tube's axis of symmetry, in the laboratory frame.

conditions.tube: square shock tube 89 mm wide; the cylinder, 50 mm in diameter, spans the tube with its centre on the tube's axis
conditions.air_ahead_of_the_shock: at rest, 101325 Pa, 1.20 kg/m^3 (perfect gas, gamma 1.4, R 287 J/(kg K))
conditions.shock: Mach 1.22 into the still air; the incident shock speeds measured in the experiments were 410 m/s (light-gas run) and 415 m/s (heavy-gas run), for calibration
conditions.cylinder: at the pressure and temperature of the air ahead of the shock; the membrane (a few tenths of a micrometre of nitrocellulose) may be neglected
conditions.measurement: spark shadowgraphs at many delays, one per run; positions read from the images and fitted into speeds on x-t diagrams; the experimenters estimated an uncertainty of about 11 per cent, larger for the refracted shock in the light gas

outputs.name: v_refracted
outputs.meaning: speed of the refracted shock inside the cylinder, on the axis

outputs.name: v_transmitted
outputs.meaning: speed of the transmitted shock that leaves the cylinder downstream, on the axis, over the first cylinder diameter behind it

outputs.name: v_upstream_interface
outputs.meaning: speed of the cylinder's upstream edge on the axis, in the first phase after the incident shock has passed it

inputs.gas: helium contaminated with air, 28 per cent air by mass by the experimenters' estimate (an estimate others place between about 6 and 48 per cent)
Refrigerant 22 (CHClF2), contamination with air estimated at 3.4 per cent by mass and neglected

label: T3
subtitle: Leads to flag 04 · a Mach 1.22 shock through helium and R22
rebuild_note: Scored with the lab's two-dimensional solver; being rebuilt natively in 3D.
